verdict.rationale: Sketch's official sketch-hq/sketch-document repository documents the .sketch format as a zipped archive of JSON data plus binary assets. A community user confirms that this zipped-JSON structure enables plugins and easy git integration outside the editor, and Sketch also says it can be integrated into workflows and server applications on any platform. missing for 10: the published schema or specification depth and licensing terms are not shown in the evidence, and there is no evidence of third-party editors reading or writing .sketch files.

support.subject: As a developer, the file format is open or documented, so my designs stay portable and toolable outside the vendor's editor

citations.quote: Sketch stores documents in `.sketch` format, a zipped archive of JSON formatted data and binary data such as images.
The file format is basically zipped json files, so there's a robust plugin ecosystem and you can do things like git integration pretty easily.
Integrate Sketch into your workflows and server applications, on any platform.
